summary: Iteration 26: Dropbox folder-reorganisation focused test round. New /app/backend/tests/test_iter26_dropbox_folders.py: 15/15 passed. iter25 regression: 16 passed + 1 non-destructive skip. All 7 requirements verified end-to-end against the live preview URL (https://field-evidence-app-1.preview.emergentagent.com) with Dropbox metadata resolved via `storage.client().files_get_metadata(...)` after `await load_dropbox()`. (A) Photo upload (POST /api/ncs/{nc_id}/evidence) + chunked 125 MB video upload (/api/uploads + /chunk + /complete) as installer Ian on Project A: db.files.paths.original starts with 'dbx:'; resolved Dropbox path is `/remedialflow/Flat 7 Oakwood Rise, SW11 4GH/Media/{YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS}_{refA}_NC-01_{photo|video}_{fileId}.{jpg|mp4}`; thumb/display/stamped variants of the photo and (when generated) the video playback copy live under `/remedialflow/_system/projects/...`. (B) projects.dropbox_folder is set on first upload and stays pinned: after PATCH /api/projects/{pidA} changed the address to '... RENAMED', the SECOND photo upload still landed in the original 'Flat 7 Oakwood Rise, SW11 4GH' folder (no 'RENAMED' in the path). (C) Two projects at the same address+postcode (Project A -> Ian, Project B -> Sam) share the exact same Media folder (A.rsplit('/',1)[0] == B.rsplit('/',1)[0]) while each path contains its own ref (refA vs refB) and neither leaks the other. (D) Cross-installer RBAC still holds: Ian GET /projects/{pidB} and GET /ncs/{ncB} return 403/404; Ian DELETE /evidence/{photo_B} returns 403/404; Sam GET /projects/{pidA} returns 403/404; installer GET /api/export/link returns 403. (E) Discard draft: DELETE /api/evidence/{fid} on a draft -> 200; db.files.status becomes 'discarded' AND the Dropbox object remains readable via files_get_metadata() (append-only guarantee). (F) ZIP export: GET /api/export/link?project_id=... returns 200 for both employee and admin; downloaded ZIP > 2 KB and contains the NC PDF; after two consecutive exports db.dropbox_exports has >=2 rows for the project, each at `/remedialflow/<folder>/<refA>/<refA>_Evidence_Pack_<stamp>_<6hex>.zip` with a 6-hex suffix matching `_[0-9a-f]{6}\.zip$`, distinct paths (no overwrite), and NOT inside Media/. The direct /api/export/project/{pid}.zip response still streams the zip unchanged (same test flow). (G) Legacy readability: a legacy Emergent-stored file was fetched 200 via its signed URL, and a legacy dbx file under /remedialflow/projects/... or /remedialflow/_system/projects/... was also fetched 200 — nothing in the old layout broke. (H) Regression: iter25 suite still passes end-to-end (RBAC, chunked flow retry/wrong-offset/early-complete/cross-user 404, Range 206 playback, zip export). No files were deleted from Dropbox; no Dropbox delete/move/overwrite API is called anywhere (verified by code review: storage.py HybridStorage only exposes put/get). Zero API returned 500.
action_items: No fixes required. New Dropbox folder layout (Media + per-ref export folder, _system for derived files, dropbox_folder pinned on project) is implemented correctly and verified against the live Dropbox app folder.
Optional: expose an admin-only read-only endpoint that returns the resolved Dropbox path per file variant (currently resolved via a direct dropbox client call in tests). Not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py:863-871 property_folder() correctly pins the folder on first use by setting dropbox_folder with the predicate {'dropbox_folder': None} — concurrent uploads on the same project cannot overwrite an existing value, and later address edits in /patch_project do NOT touch dropbox_folder (verified: PATCH address + new upload stayed in the original folder).

/app/backend/storage.py:158-174 property_folder_name() appends ', POSTCODE' only when the postcode is missing from the address and uppercases the postcode; media_path() and export_path() embed the file_id / 6-hex uid respectively so Dropbox 'add' mode is guaranteed collision-free (append-only).

/app/backend/server.py:874-885 save_export_copy() is best-effort (try/except with audit entry on failure) and runs as a BackgroundTask after the ZIP is returned to the client — the user never waits for the Dropbox copy, and failure cannot corrupt the download path.

/app/backend/server.py:909-912 store_upload() routes photo/video originals to media_path() under the property's shared folder; everything else (TrustMark reference images, derived variants) goes to evidence_path() under {APP_NAME}/_system/projects/... as required.

/app/backend/server.py:984-997 discard_evidence() only flips files.status to 'discarded' — storage.py has no delete/move/overwrite API — so no user action can ever remove a Dropbox object (confirmed in tests: Dropbox metadata still readable after DELETE).
